title: perf(canary): tighten auto-detection thresholds + hysteresis for rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description:
Background: the perf-canary service runs continuous latency/throughput detection and gates model rollouts via rollout guards. We've seen noisy false positives when transient spikes exceed static thresholds and cases where hysteresis prevented recovery after transient regressions. Motivation: improve precision of automated detection, reduce noisy rollback/hold events, and ensure safe automatic recovery.

What this PR does: single continuous body describing changes:
- Introduces adaptive thresholding: signal-specific baseline windows (p95/p99 latency and qps) and dynamic multiplier instead of fixed thresholds.
- Adds hysteresis windows for both detection and recovery phases to avoid flip-flop rollouts.
- Improves statistical test: switch from simple percent-change compare to bootstrapped confidence interval for latency deltas and Poisson test for throughput.
- Exposes new config knobs with safe defaults in config/defaults.yaml and runtime tuning via the console.
- Adds a diagnostic endpoint (/perf-canary/debug) returning last N decisions for debugging.
- Adds unit + e2e tests simulating transient spikes, slow steady regressions, and flapping.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (ENG-2345) linked
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests for canary detector
- [x] Console controls wired (read-only rollout guard view)
- [x] Updated changelog & release notes

Risk: algorithm changes alter sensitivity; safe defaults are conservative and we added a feature-flag (perf_canary_v2_detection) to toggle. Rolling back is a config flip.

How to test locally: run perf-canary simulator with --scenario=transient-spike and --scenario=steady-regression (see tools/perf-canary/sim).

References: ENG-2345 (design), incident SUP-4123 (noisy rollouts from last month).

changes_summary:
Key algorithm changes (snippets):
- adaptive baseline window: baseline := computeWindow(metrics, cfg.BaselineWindowMinutes)
- bootstrap CI: deltaCI := bootstrapDelta(prevSamples, currSamples, cfg.BootstrapIter)
- hysteresis state machine: if detect && consecutive >= cfg.HysteresisDetectCount -> hold/rollback; if recovered && consecutiveRecover >= cfg.HysteresisRecoverCount -> resume

Small example: detector.go - new decision path:
+ if deltaCI.Lower > cfg.MaxAllowedIncrease { return Decision{Action: 'pause', reason: 'latency_regression_confident'} }
+ else if poissonP < cfg.ThroughputPValue { return Decision{Action: 'pause', reason: 'throughput_drop_significant'} }

release_notes: Improved perf canary detection: adaptive thresholds, hysteresis for rollouts, and more robust statistical tests to reduce noisy rollbacks. Feature gated behind perf_canary_v2_detection.
